script_data.topic: Why do your fingers wrinkle in water?
script_data.title: This Is Why Your Fingers Wrinkle
script_data.voiceover: Why do your fingers wrinkle? You assume your skin just acts like a dry sponge absorbing a bath. That soggy sponge theory completely falls apart when you look at nerve damage. Water triggers your autonomic nervous system to actively shrink the blood vessels. This rapid blood loss forces the outer layer of skin to collapse downward. Your body does this on purpose to create an efficient wet surface traction system. Pruney fingers act like tire treads, squeezing water out to grip wet objects better.
